currency_assumptions: Native prices are THB. The USD comparison uses USD 1 = THB 33.93 on 2026-11-24 (Frankfurter, the last business day before the check), so THB 1 = USD 0.02947244.
Published rates are starting or day rates, not all-in quotes; the True Digital Park sheet states its prices exclude 7% VAT, and catering, staffing and AV extras are not quantified by any operator.
A published day rate is converted only for a window the cited page publishes; no programme cost is claimed while the window is unknown.
The soft budget is USD 5,000; exactly 5,000 is not over budget and cost is never a gate.

declared_gaps.text: All 44 records carry numeric pins: 3 exact_venue (Samyan Mitrtown Hall, Warehouse 30 and IMPACT Arena - each the venue's own single OSM object), 33 building, 2 street (HUBBA Sathorn and WeLearn) and 6 area (the six True Digital Park rooms). Ten records share three building/complex points - four Lido Connect rooms, four QSNCC rooms and two BITEC rooms - and are labelled building, not exact_venue, because one shared point cannot claim a verified room entrance; the Kuala Lumpur and Lisbon room groups are labelled the same way. No room-level entrance was verified for any record.

Seven records cannot be pinned finer than an area or a street. True Digital Park's six event rooms sit on a campus with no tower-level OSM object, so the pin is the campus. HUBBA Sathorn's printed number 4 is not in the OSM index, so the pin is the Naradhiwas Rajanagarindra Road segment. WeLearn's printed 「16 Phraya Phiren Alley」 returns no OSM object for the number or the alley spelling, but 「Soi Phraya Phiren」 resolves to OSM way 53271857 in the same subdistrict and postcode (Thung Maha Mek, Sathon 10120), so the pin is that street and the house number stays unmatched. The IMPACT halls use the complex/building objects because the operator prints only its Bangkok Land Building head office.

Photos after the refresh: 38 venues with 1+, 14 with 4+, 6 with none; 108 live rows drawn from 38 distinct images, plus 6 explicit withheld records. Of the 108 live rows, 83 are exterior or complex fallbacks and 25 are room-side: 4 show the record's own room, 11 another room in the same hotel or complex, 5 the hotel lobby and 5 building circulation or entrance interiors. 11 of the 14 venues at 4+ have no photo of their own room: the four QSNCC rooms each carry the same four building images, the two BITEC rooms, Samyan Mitrtown Hall, Warehouse 30 and IMPACT Arena carry building or exterior sets, and Regency Room and Embassy Room carry other Mandarin Oriental rooms and the lobby. Rights mix: 8 CC BY 3.0, 9 CC BY 4.0, 5 CC BY-SA 2.0 de, 21 CC BY-SA 3.0, 65 CC BY-SA 4.0. No operator room gallery with a stated licence was found; the five cleared room files are Wikimedia Commons images (Mandarin Oriental Royal Ballroom, Sala Rim Naam and Authors' Lounge; River City Artery and Auctions Room) and are reused across records in the same building, so they do not map one-to-one to the 25 room-side rows; the remaining rows are lobby, building-interior or another room's file.

The 20 Bank of Thailand financial-institution rows were removed. The government layer is built from the standing HM Prime Minister's Office announcement B.E. 2562 (19 annual holidays, Royal Gazette vol. 136, special part 135 Ngor, 27 May 2019); the Cabinet resolution acknowledging the B.E. 2570 overview and any special replacement days had not been issued as at 2026-11-26, so the four lunar rows (21 February, 20 May, 18 July, 19 July) and the three substitute days (22 February, 25 October, 6 December) are rule-derived, carry verified false and subject_to_announcement, and are not read from a 2570 table. No Asalha substitute is stored: 19 July is Khao Phansa and Thai PBS prints three government substitutes, so the Asalha substitute remains unresolved. Royal Ploughing Ceremony is pending. Bangkok-specific municipal closures could not be retrieved (BMA portal 403).

The school layer has two 2027 term-break rows derived from the Ministry of Education school-year regulation B.E. 2549 (clauses 6-7); the BMA Department of Education order for academic year 2569 returned a Cloudflare 403, so no dated BMA table was read. No private or international-school calendar was substituted. 2027 coverage is stated in the coverage rows; 2028 is not attested.

Six 2027 events are retained. The six-theme matrix was attempted across Luma city/alias/organiser, Meetup, Eventbrite, the three MiraGather views and AI Tinkerers (54 cells). ML yielded nothing physical: ICMLAS 2027 says it will be held online. Crypto and blockchain yielded no confirmed Bangkok 2027 edition: SEA Blockchain Week's domain is parked with dates TBA, Thailand Crypto Expo did not resolve, and the WASET blockchain conference returned 403. MiraGather's three views and the Decentralized AI lane returned shells (0 pages read).

Access split: 3 full 09:00-21:00 (the three True Digital Park Grand Hall configurations), 3 floor-only 8-hour (True Digital Park Training Room 1, Training Room 3 and Classroom 7, published 08:00-18:00), 1 shorter (River City RCB Forum, published 10:00-20:00, which does not fit the 09:00 start), 37 unknown. Every yes cites the published clock line; no hotel banqueting prose was promoted to a window.

Address forms vary: QSNCC's directory-only 「60 Queen Sirikit National Convention Center」 was replaced by 60 Ratchadaphisek Road; the IMPACT halls carry the complex name because the operator prints only its head office; The Jam Factory address comes from a directory page because the operator domain did not resolve; HUBBA's printed line has no soi; WeLearn prints only 「16 Phraya Phiren Alley」, whose street resolves in the OSM index while the house number does not. The Banquet Halls record's inherited 「101-102」 suffix was dropped because no captured operator line carries it; the page names the two Banquet Halls inside IMPACT Forum Hall 4. All other addresses were re-read against the operator capture on 2026-11-26.
No venue was contacted and no site visit was made; the visits list stays empty.

alcohol.quote:
Two acts regulate the manufacturing, import and sale of alcoholic beverages in Thailand. It concerns the Liquor Act of 1950 and the Alcoholic Beverage Control Act of 2008. The first defines the term spirit or liquor as any material or mixture that contains alcohol and is consumable or becomes consumable after mixing with water or other liquids.
The Excise Department is not only responsible to collect the excise tax on alcohol; they are also the regulatory agency for alcohol production and distribution (in accordance with the Liquor Act B.E. 2493). The licensing system of the Excise Department obliges the licensee to sell the above-mentioned alcoholic beverages in line with Thai regulation.
The Liquor Act prohibits license holders to sell alcoholic beverages: a) to people younger than 20 years or those people that lose their consciousness when they drink; b) between 12 pm and 11 am and from 2 pm to 5 pm and c) ‘within’ or ‘next to’ educational and religious areas.
alcohol.source_locator: Liquor Act B.E. 2493 summary: regulator, licence to sell, sale-hour rule
alcohol.source_title: Import alcohol to Thailand: Alcohol license | Acclime

translation_review.gloss: The Liquor Act of 1950 and the Alcoholic Beverage Control Act of 2008 govern alcohol. The Excise Department licenses production and distribution under the Liquor Act B.E. 2493, and a seller must hold a licence. The Act restricts sales to people under 20 and during stated hours, and near educational and religious sites.
translation_review.review: This is a law-firm summary, not the statute text, and its sale-hour sentence is garbled in transcription ('between 12 pm and 11 am and from 2 pm to 5 pm'), so no hour window is asserted from it. The reliable points are that a licence is required to sell and that the Excise Department is the regulator.

value.observed_rule: Selling alcohol needs an Excise Department licence and is subject to statutory sale hours; a hotel's own licence and an event licence are separate questions.
value.unknown: Who holds the licence for each room, whether it covers a closed 50-person event, the permitted serving hours to 21:00 and any district-level enforcement difference.
value.venue_level: Where an operator prints a bar it is noted; alcohol_service stays unknown on all 30 assessed rooms rather than assumed.

verification_questions: Ask each venue who holds the licence, whether it covers a closed private event, and the permitted serving hours to 21:00.

food.quote: If you plan to sell or import alcohol in Thailand, you will have to acquire an alcohol license in order to operate your business legally.
food.source_locator: Opening statement of the alcohol-licensing guide, read only to confirm that no food rule is in it
food.source_title: Import alcohol to Thailand: Alcohol license | Acclime

value.observed_rule: No Thai food-safety or catering-licence authority was retrieved. The quoted line is the alcohol guide's opening sentence and is recorded only as proof of what that page does and does not cover; no food rule is asserted from it.
value.unknown: Which caterers each venue approves, whether external catering is allowed, and what Thai food-premises registration applies.
value.venue_level: catering, food_service and delivery_allowed stay unknown on every room.

verification_questions: Confirm the venue's approved caterers and any external-catering fee.
